races.name: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden
Bulmers Live At Leopardstown Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Faoladh
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner mapping comfortably to its natural prominent role; won over this exact C&D trip on good ground 8 days ago and has a strong sim-going record, though the STYLE_FIT tag notes it is fractionally out of pure lead role — nonetheless it controls the race entirely from the front.
runners_data.comment: Faoladh won three starts back and has raced over today's distance before, returning quickly here just eight days after his latest run; rated third of 14 with a strong speed figure, the drawback is a yard managing only 1/33 in the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Ardeur
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with a poor recent string including two last-place finishes; sim-going record is thin at 4 from 10 and the step back from 8f to 7f is untested in winning form, making her a very speculative late player.
runners_data.comment: Ardeur is winless in her last five starts, three of them unplaced, and a 28-day gap since her latest run raises a fitness question. She does have experience over today's trip, which keeps her competitive without standing out from this field.

runners_data.name: Comfort Line
runners_data.note: Veteran 9-year-old prominent racer with genuine course form — has placed twice over 7f on good ground and won over 8f on Standard; blinkers fitted (hg:v) likely to sharpen focus and the 13-day return looks acceptable for Adrian McGuinness's stable which is firing at 2/33.
runners_data.comment: Comfort Line won three starts back and has raced over today's distance before, following that win with a solid second next time out; he faded to a below-par fifth last time out, and the question is whether that was a blip or a genuine downturn.

runners_data.name: God Knows
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who has placed twice at 8f-10f on good ground but struggles over shorter; the 62-day layoff and recent form string showing a string of poor returns limit confidence here, though good ground suits.
runners_data.comment: God Knows tops our figures by a clear margin, form built on two runner-up efforts earlier in her recent sequence; the concern is a 62-day layoff since her latest run and a string of below-par efforts in between that leave her placing here slightly open to question.

runners_data.name: Rodeeve
runners_data.note: True hold-up type whose natural running style places it at the rear, mapped here to midfield due to field congestion — its best win came over 6f on good ground and it has a place at 7f; the STYLE_FIT flag at 0.92 tempers expectations if it cannot get its preferred position.
runners_data.comment: Rodeeve won two starts back and has raced over today's distance before, but followed that form with an unplaced effort last time out; a quick 15-day turnaround keeps her ticking over, leaving the task of proving that win wasn't a one-off.

runners_data.name: Ardadslosttheplot
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up racer who has placed twice over 7f on good ground and filled third last time out 12 days ago; Rebecca Parsons rides for David Marnane whose stable is at 1/17 in the 14-day window, and the distance and going combination look fair.
runners_data.comment: Ardadslosttheplot is yet to score in her last five starts but has been placed twice in that run, third again last time out, and a 12-day turnaround keeps her ticking over; the question is whether she has the class edge to go one better here.

runners_data.name: Dynamic Force
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with a very strong sim-going profile (13 from 15 on good) but drawn into midfield here because there are simply too many hold-up runners — its natural rear-of-field position is compromised, which the 0.93 STYLE_FIT reflects; no wins in last five.
runners_data.comment: Dynamic Force has been largely consistent without a win, mostly in the first seven bar one unplaced effort, and a 13-day turnaround keeps him ticking over; the drawback is a yard well below form at just 1/22 in the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Bear Right
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with three places in last five starts over 7f-8f on good or good-to-soft; has headgear fitted (hg:p), races hold-up but has placed from a tracking position — Mrs John Harrington's yard is at 1/28 in 14 days, returning after 15 days.
runners_data.comment: Bear Right has strung together three solid efforts, placed twice and no worse than fourth, form that points to a filly finding her feet at the right time; the concern is a yard well below its recent strike-rate, just 1/28 in the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Prime Sign
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a pronounced fade-in-finish flag and a run just 5 days ago; the sim-going record is modest and recent form shows a 24th at 7f on good — redistributed to midfield but unlikely to improve on that without a significant step forward.
runners_data.comment: Prime Sign has managed only one finish inside the top half of her last five starts, down the field again in ninth last time out, so the recent record is hard to overlook; a quick five-day turnaround is about the only thing working in her favour here.

runners_data.name: Frosted Sky
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old with only three runs, all finishing 6th, 8th, 8th — no form at this distance and a finish-fade flag; bumped to midfield in the map but a genuine hold-up type stepping up markedly in experience, with Daniel McLoughlin's yard striking at 2/10.

runners_data.name: Cordouan
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up runner whose best sim-going finish is 8th from 15 tries — placed in pattern is sparse and last run was 66 days ago; natural position is at the rear, displaced to midfield here, and confidence is low at OR 53.
runners_data.comment: Cordouan's finishing positions read modestly, no better than eighth in his last five starts, but the form conceals a strong speed figure that hints at more to come; a 66-day absence since his latest run is the obvious fitness concern.

runners_data.name: Mehmar
runners_data.note: Hold-up six-year-old drawn across multiple trip distances in recent form including a 12th and an 8th; lacks a win on good ground and the sim-going record (6 from 15) offers little encouragement — Jack Cleary's mount at the lowest OR in the field.
runners_data.comment: Mehmar's finishing positions have been modest, no better than fifth in his last six starts, yet a notably strong speed figure suggests more untapped ability than the bare results show; question marks remain over whether that will translate into a leading role here.

runners_data.name: Notforalongtime
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with genuine placed form on good ground (three places in last five over 7f-8f) and a natural hold-up style; Rory Mulligan takes the ride and the horse has been consistent without threatening — placed from the rear is its ceiling rather than a win.
runners_data.comment: Notforalongtime has been well held in three of his last six starts, eighth again last time out, leaving plenty to find on the bare results; a pair of thirds earlier is the one genuine positive, though he ranks near the bottom on these figures.

runners_data.name: Smaoineamh Sile
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up eight-year-old with a fade-in-finish flag and form almost entirely built on Standard/Tapeta surfaces; form string includes a unseated rider and two zeros, and the sim-going record (7 from 15 on good) suggests the switch to turf good is a real concern.
runners_data.comment: Smaoineamh Sile's recent form reads unseated, unplaced three times and a best of eighth, with nothing to suggest a leading role in this field; she sits bottom of the fourteen runners on these figures, though a prompt reappearance at least keeps her ticking over.

runners_data.name: Dawn Flame
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type running for the second time in five days with a finish-fade flag; has placed once over 6f on good ground but form at 7f-8f is poor, and while Paul W Flynn's yard is in solid 14-day form (4/25), the horse's own record limits expectations.
runners_data.comment: Dawn Flame found a definite lift last time out, coming home third after a mixed run of finishes in his last six starts; the concern is a modest underlying speed figure that leaves him needing that step forward repeated rather than a one-off.

races.paceDynamic: Faoladh is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 15-horse field at 7f on good ground at Leopardstown, and with no genuine rival disputing the lead, Sam Coen can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front without expending energy in a pace battle. The field is overwhelmingly populated by hold-up and midfield types, meaning Faoladh sets the tempo entirely on its own terms — the pace is unlikely to be genuinely strong, which compresses the finish and makes it harder for true closers to generate the momentum they need. Several horses tagged as redistributed — Rodeeve, Frosted Sky, Dynamic Force, Prime Sign, Cordouan, Mehmar, Notforalongtime, Smaoineamh Sile and Dawn Flame — are genuine hold-up types who cannot all find their natural deep position in a field this large, meaning some will race closer than ideal, further muddying late sectionals. This race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently behind the leader or race in the first third of the field, as the modest pace set by a lone front-runner on good ground at Leopardstown will reward those who stay in touch throughout rather than those relying on a late burst from well off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Faoladh Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Faoladh bowls along at a controlled pace and the chasing pack fail to close the gap until it is too late.
scenarios.body: Faoladh, uncontested up front, dictates a moderate gallop that suits its stamina profile at 7f on good ground, and with no horse applying early pressure, it can conserve energy through the middle section before quickening clear late. Prominent racers who track Faoladh closely — particularly Comfort Line and Ardadslosttheplot — are best placed to challenge, but the advantage lies with the horse in front controlling the fractions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Chasers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine enough to stretch Faoladh in the final furlong, allowing a prominent tracker to sweep past close home.
scenarios.body: Comfort Line, a veteran course performer who has placed twice over this trip on good ground, can sit a close second and pounce when Faoladh's effort levels in the final 100 yards; Ardadslosttheplot, who showed good form at 7f on good ground when third, is another that could benefit from this shape. This scenario suits those racing in the first four or five at halfway who can unleash a late kick without needing a searching pace to set it up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Runner Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slightly stronger than expected and a midfield horse sustains its run through the final two furlongs to catch tiring leaders.
scenarios.body: Bear Right, who has placed three times over similar trips and can travel comfortably in mid-division, is the likeliest beneficiary if legs start to tire in front; Ardeur has the profile to close late on good ground having shown some ability at this level. This scenario is moderately discounted because so many of the nominal midfield occupants are redistributed hold-up types who may not produce the sustained finishing effort the shape requires.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Storm Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace somehow becomes significantly stronger, opening the race up for true hold-up horses coming from deep.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely outcome given Faoladh's unchallenged lead and the near-certain moderate gallop; even if a redistributed horse like Rodeeve or God Knows finds a clear run, the compressed finish on a controlled pace leaves minimal room for deep closers to deliver their best. The high STYLE_FIT discounts and multiple redistribution flags across this group make a late-sweeping winner the lowest-probability shape in this race.

watchPoints.text: Faoladh sets every fraction unchallenged — watch whether Sam Coen allows a genuine gallop or throttles back so severely that the field bunches behind, as that is the pivotal tactical variable in this race.

Comfort Line and Ardadslosttheplot are the most likely horses to apply pressure in the straight — if either tracks Faoladh within two lengths at the furlong pole, the lead could be swallowed up quickly on good ground at Leopardstown.

Multiple redistributed hold-up types — including Rodeeve, Dynamic Force and Frosted Sky — may push forward out of their comfort zone in the first two furlongs as riders jostle for position in a 15-runner field, which could briefly spike the early pace before the field settles.

Bear Right carries headgear and has consistent place form over 7f-8f; watch how Keithen Kennedy positions it at halfway, as a prominent mid-race move could make it a factor if the race compresses late.

Prime Sign and Dawn Flame both carry finish-fade flags and have run very recently (5 days); if either appears prominent in early exchanges, expect them to weaken significantly inside the final two furlongs.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
Dublin To Bahrain Handicap

runners_data.name: Aviatrice
runners_data.note: Won twice from a prominent position in similar good-ground conditions and steps up to a mile — a trip she has already won over — arriving in decent recent form, making her the most naturally placed horse to exploit How'sthebai's likely front-running role.
runners_data.comment: Aviatrice is rated top of seven on our figures at 94 with a useful speed figure of 83 in support, having won two of her last five starts and been placed in two of the other three. Fit again just 19 days after her latest run, she remains the biggest threat on pure form.

runners_data.name: Loughrea
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery trains and rides in a dual role that worked well at Gowran last time; two placed runs on good ground at this distance suit the flat mile perfectly, and a prominent style means she should never be far off the pace.
runners_data.comment: Loughrea won last time out, having been runner-up two starts back, a clearly progressive sort with the trip and recent fitness both in his favour. The yard is a little out of form (1/33 in the last fortnight), but his upward curve makes him our selection.

runners_data.name: Exquisite Acclaim
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old hold-up specialist who needs the race truly run to be effective; headgear (visor) and a short eight-day turnaround noted, and his similar-going record (0 wins, 1 place from 15) makes him hard to trust at the top of the market.
runners_data.comment: Exquisite Acclaim is rated mid-pack on our figures at 87, having won six starts back but form has been mixed since, including two unplaced efforts in that time. A quick reappearance just 8 days on, and the trip already covered, keep him firmly in contention rather than a standout.

runners_data.name: How'sthebai
runners_data.note: Confirmed as the lone pace-setter yet the STYLE_FIT flag indicates this is a horse that more naturally settles rather than leads — Keane may push him forward but the rating of 90 is earned in a different tactical context, so discount his chance if the lead role drains him.
runners_data.comment: How'sthebai has won twice in his last five starts, most recently two starts back, and is rated fourth of seven on our figures at 90 with a strong speed figure of 83. A stray sixth further back is the only blot, but with the trip already covered he remains a big threat on his best form.

runners_data.name: Quatre Bras
runners_data.note: Ran just three days ago which is the shortest turnaround in the field; genuinely prominent by inclination, he has been pushed back to a midfield position on the race map because more forward types than the front can hold are present — if he breaks quickly he could reclaim his preferred ground but current form figures (040884) are uninspiring.
runners_data.comment: Quatre Bras is rated bottom of seven on our figures at 85 and winless in his last six starts, with only a pair of modest fourths to show. A rapid reappearance just 3 days on keeps him fresh, but there's little in this form to inspire real confidence.

runners_data.name: Invincible Will
runners_data.note: Best form comes as a closer on good ground — a course win over 7f at Leopardstown demonstrates track familiarity — and the 7-day turnaround following an eighth-place run suggests connections are keen; needs a strong enough gallop to manufacture his late run, which this shape may not fully supply.
runners_data.comment: Invincible Will was runner-up last time and is rated third of seven on our figures at 92, with a win three starts back among a mixed sequence. He backs up quickly just 7 days later, though the yard is a little out of form (1/45 in the last fortnight) - the one concern on an otherwise solid profile.

runners_data.name: Tachos
runners_data.note: A true prominent racer whose natural position cannot be secured in this competitive shape, mapped to midfield as a result; best form came at shorter trips on a variety of going and the OR of 75 as the lowest-rated runner makes finding the winner hard from this position.
runners_data.comment: Tachos is rated second-bottom of seven on our figures at 85 and winless in her last five starts, without threatening the frame once in that time. A useful speed figure of 81 hints at some ability, but on the form alone she has plenty to prove.

races.paceDynamic: How'sthebai is the lone confirmed front runner and, with no genuine rival disputing the lead, is set to control the pace from the outset at a sustainable, self-dictated tempo over this flat mile at Leopardstown. That controlled early gallop will likely produce a race where position is currency — prominent racers who can sit just off the leader and maintain contact through the middle stages are best placed to strike. This field contains more prominent types than the front of the race can accommodate: Quatre Bras and Tachos are genuine front-running or prominent horses by nature but have been mapped to midfield because Aviatrice and Loughrea are better placed to secure their preferred positions in this shape. A steady, uncontested pace with a compressed field approaching the straight strongly favours horses racing prominently — those who can track the leader and produce their effort early in the home straight — rather than true hold-up types who will need a strong gallop to generate the gaps they require.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If How'sthebai sets a controlled solo lead and Aviatrice or Loughrea track closely to pounce turning in.
scenarios.body: How'sthebai's uncontested, unhurried gallop creates a steadily-run mile where the horses sitting second and third have the race set up perfectly for them; those with the tactical speed to quicken off a modest pace will dominate.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If How'sthebai dictates an even pace and the field fails to close through a flat, uncontested home straight.
scenarios.body: A single front runner with no pressure can conserve enough energy to outstay challengers when the pace has been metronomic; Colin Keane's positioning and experience makes this a live alternative.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sufficiently through the middle of the race to string the field out and create a genuine run-in.
scenarios.body: Invincible Will has the profile to finish powerfully if the race develops into a proper test, with his best form coming when able to close late on good ground; Exquisite Acclaim is another that needs the race truly run to get competitive.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Type Capitalises
scenarios.trigger: If Quatre Bras or Tachos manages to break smartly and reclaim their natural prominent position despite the field's composition.
scenarios.body: These horses are genuine forwardly-placed types by inclination and if the race shape allows one of them to slot in ahead of expectations they could outrun their reassigned roles; the probability is marked down significantly because their mapped positions reflect genuine competition for ground at the front.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether How'sthebai actually commits to the lead from the gate — if Colin Keane elects to settle him rather than force the pace, the entire race shape collapses and the field will have no true pacesetter.

Quatre Bras runs for the second time in four days; if fatigue sets in after a fast early break the field behind him could be bunched and a messy race unfolds, particularly affecting Invincible Will and Exquisite Acclaim's ability to find a clear run.

Aviatrice carries 140lbs — the highest weight in the race — and while her form entitles her to that mark, the combination of top weight and a mile at Leopardstown on unknown going deserves monitoring as the race develops.

Loughrea's trainer-jockey combination (Andrew Slattery dual role) is low-profile but has recorded a 3% strike rate over 14 days; worth watching whether the booking of Slattery to ride his own horse signals significant stable confidence following back-to-back placings.

races.name: BOYLE Sports Meld Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Adelaide River
runners_data.note: JP O'Brien-trained six-year-old with strong recent Leopardstown form and a 1W4P record on similar going; McMonagle is an aggressive pace-tracking jockey who will look to sit second to Geryon and that prominent role is entirely natural for this horse — the danger is she may simply be outclassed at the top end of a Group 3.
runners_data.comment: Adelaide River is rated top of six on our figures at 114, having been placed twice in his last five starts with today's trip under his belt. Yet to score in that time, and below-par when unplaced last time after a 30-day break.

runners_data.name: Cowardofthecounty
runners_data.note: The only genuine hold-up horse in this small field, this JP O'Brien four-year-old needs a hot pace that Geryon is unlikely to provide; recent form shows a win over 7f on good ground but stepping up to 1m1f for the first time in this company is a significant ask, and without pace collapse the tactical situation is stacked against her.
runners_data.comment: Cowardofthecounty was placed last time out and a winner two starts back, though a couple of below-par efforts further back leave him hard to fully trust; our figures rate him second-bottom of six at 102, only modest on speed at 78.

runners_data.name: Snellen
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's five-year-old is a confirmed prominent racer by style, yet the surplus of pace-side types in this field means Gary Carroll will almost certainly find himself further back than ideal — a genuine front-ranker shunted into a role that does not suit; his excellent 15/15 sim-going record signals conditions are right, but the positional compromise is a real cost.
runners_data.comment: Snellen was a winner four starts back and placed two starts back, form that reads well; a below-par fifth last time is the one concern, but with the trip under her belt and our figures rating her second of six at 111, she rates a solid alternative.

runners_data.name: Syzygy
runners_data.note: Daniel McLoughlin's four-year-old carries a blinkers flag and, like Snellen, is a true pace-side horse whose natural berth has been displaced by the field's composition; Ben Coen will need to be creative to find a position, and a modest 0W2P record on similar going (good) does nothing to compensate for the tactical awkwardness.
runners_data.comment: She was runner-up last time; a winner five starts back remains the pick of her form, but a 39-day absence and a mixed set of efforts in between make her harder to fancy. Our figures rate Syzygy bottom of six at 97, slowest of these on speed at 77.

runners_data.name: Geryon
runners_data.note: The race-shaper: GM Lyons's lightly-weighted three-year-old with Colin Keane up will roll to the front and is confirmed as the sole front-runner; six of his last seven runs have been on similar going and he has shown a consistent ability to sit just off the pace or lead, though his overall record of 1W3P suggests he has not always delivered when it matters — the key question is whether this controlled scenario finally brings out his best.
runners_data.comment: Geryon is rated third of six on our figures at 107 with solid speed to match at 93, twice runner-up in his last five starts. Still without a win in that time, but fresh off just an 18-day break, he looks a big threat.

runners_data.name: Isaac Newton
runners_data.note: AP O'Brien's three-year-old won over 9f on good ground and holds smart form, but his natural prominent style cannot be fully expressed in a field this congested with similar types — Wayne Lordan will find himself shuffled back despite the horse's instincts; a STYLE_FIT discount applies, and recent form (4-4516) including a sixth last time is modest, though an OR of 105 keeps him in the picture if the scenario breaks right.
runners_data.comment: Only sixth last time, Isaac Newton won two starts back, and with the trip already covered plus useful efforts either side, he can't be dismissed; our figures rate him fourth of six at 103, backed by a solid speed figure of 92.

races.paceDynamic: Geryon is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with just six runners over 1m1f at Leopardstown, Colin Keane will be able to dictate an unchallenged, metronomic gallop from the front — there is no rival willing or able to pressure him early. Adelaide River will look to press from a prominent berth and is the only horse likely to genuinely share the early lead, but she lacks the raw pace to force a true test, meaning Geryon controls tempo entirely. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — Snellen, Isaac Newton, and Syzygy are all natural pace-side horses who will be squeezed into a midfield role they do not naturally suit, making their tasks harder. This race shape firmly favours horses who can track a controlled pace and produce a sustained late run — a prominent-to-midfield tracker or a horse with a strong finishing kick from just off the pace is the profile that benefits most here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Geryon Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Geryon's uncontested lead produces a steady, controlled gallop that fails to fully bring out closers.
scenarios.body: Keane rolls Geryon to the front unchallenged, sets an honest but not punishing tempo, and the horse's natural relaxed racing style allows it to conserve enough energy to resist late challengers into the Leopardstown straight; at OR 106 with strong good-ground form (6/7 sim-going) and a younger horse's residual freshness, it has the class to sustain.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just steady enough to allow a well-positioned tracker to swoop in the final furlong without blowing up.
scenarios.body: Adelaide River, tracking Geryon closely from the second position, gets the perfect rails-run into the straight and picks up when the leader tires, her strong 1W4P record at similar going validating the trip and conditions; McMonagle's aggressive front-rank riding style means she rarely gets caught flat-footed when the race quickens.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or accelerates sharply enough in the straight to catch the leader but reward a late, sustained run from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Isaac Newton or Snellen, racing against their natural prominent instincts from a midfield berth, gets a clean passage into the straight and benefits if the front two tire; both carry STYLE_FIT discounts and their redistribution to midfield works against them, but OR 105 ratings mean they hold the class to feature if the shape breaks their way.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If a truly fast early tempo develops and decimates the front end, handing the race to a genuine closer.
scenarios.body: Cowardofthecounty is the only authentic hold-up runner in the field and would benefit uniquely from a collapse of the front-runners, but with Geryon likely to face zero early pressure this scenario is highly unlikely; the horse's recent form (0-8213) and drop back from sprint distances also temper expectations.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Snellen, Isaac Newton, or Syzygy attempt to challenge Geryon for the lead in the first furlong — if any of them do, the entire pace dynamic shifts from a controlled solo lead to a contested gallop that could open the race up for Cowardofthecounty.

Monitor Geryon's early splits: if Keane sets a genuinely slow tempo through the first half-mile, the race risks turning into a sprint finish that negates class differences and could flatter any of the midfield types who find cover.

Adelaide River's positioning in the first two furlongs is critical — if McMonagle cannot secure second place directly behind Geryon and gets squeezed back by the redistributed prominent horses, her race is effectively over before the straight.

Cowardofthecounty is worth tracking for market moves close to post time; a hold-up horse in a race with one confirmed front-runner is at structural disadvantage, but if punters have intelligence on a faster-than-expected pace, late support here would be meaningful.

Isaac Newton ran in a Grade 1 at the Curragh last time and drops back significantly in class today — watch whether AP O'Brien's team view this as a confidence-restoring opportunity or a genuine Group 3 target, as the jockey booking of Wayne Lordan rather than Ryan Moore is a notable downgrade worth factoring.

races.name: Mervue Equine Handicap

runners_data.name: En Or
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who has not raced for 43 days and steps back to 1m2f, which is shorter than his recent assignments at 14-16f; eight-year-old carrying 144lbs but a clean bill of health on Good ground and, if he bowls along uncontested, his chance of lasting home is greater here than the long trips suggest.
runners_data.comment: En Or ranks second in the field on our figures with a leading speed figure to match, giving him solid claims on ability; the query is recent form, nothing better than seventh in his last five starts, plus a 43-day absence since his latest run.

runners_data.name: Daler
runners_data.note: Four-year-old in good recent form with a win at 9f on soft and a placed effort at 10f on Good; Colin Keane rides and trainer Lyons is 5/23 in the last 14 days — the step up to 1m2f looks like the key question, and his prominent style means he should be in a good position throughout.
runners_data.comment: Daler won two starts back and confirmed that form with a close second last time out, making him the one to beat here on our figures; the only query is finding the same level again after a quieter spell earlier in the sequence.

runners_data.name: Unterberg
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old whose recent form figures of 511108 show three wins at 10-12f on Standard, with a run on Good ground returning a modest eighth; the step back to turf and Good going is uncertain but he's clearly in form and the 1m2f trip suits.
runners_data.comment: Unterberg strung together three wins in a row earlier in his recent form, form that gives him a leading claim in this race; the concern is a sharp dip since, culminating in an eighth last time out, a marked fall from that purple patch.

runners_data.name: Marmeladova
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly with eight of her nine career runs on Good ground and an excellent placed record at 10-12f — last time out she was second over this exact trip on Good, and the consistent finishing pattern makes her the most natural beneficiary of a steady pace set by En Or.
runners_data.comment: Marmeladova has been on an upward curve - a win four starts back, then successive placed efforts of fourth, third and second - and a rapid nine-day turnaround keeps her fighting fit; the query is finding the extra to convert those places into victory here.

runners_data.name: Neo Smart
runners_data.note: Prominent-style five-year-old whose recent form at 8f on Good has been moderate, but he steps up to 1m2f for the first time in this sequence; J S Bolger sends him out on a light 14-day schedule and the extra distance is the key unknown.
runners_data.comment: Neo Smart won five starts back but form dipped sharply after that, with a ninth and back-to-back sevenths in between; last time's fourth suggests she may be finding some of that spark again, and a 20-day gap should keep her fresh.

runners_data.name: Sinbad My Dad
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with stamina form over 10f on Standard surfaces but a limited record on Good ground (4/15 comparable runs); the apprentice claim of seven pounds via Joseph Harnett is a practical benefit, though the going record is a mild concern.
runners_data.comment: Sinbad My Dad was placed in each of his first two starts but has since dropped away to ninth and eighth, with a modest sixth last time out the only sign of recovery; the drop in form leaves him needing to rediscover his best.

runners_data.name: Faro Island
runners_data.note: In good form at 10-12f on Good ground with two wins at those trips — a natural prominent-running type who is unlikely to secure that position in this field given the presence of En Or and multiple prominent rivals, so his best chance comes from sitting closer than ideal to the pace without his true style being fully expressed.
runners_data.comment: Faro Island has two wins in his last five starts, but they came either side of markedly worse efforts, and last time's seventh continues that indifferent pattern; the win history is the redeeming feature, though our figures rate him only modestly for this task.

runners_data.name: Out On Friday
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up horse who is flagged for fading in the finish, and whose recent Good-ground form over 10-12f shows mostly double-figure finishes; the staying concern and finishing tendency make him a very low-probability runner whatever shape the race takes.
runners_data.comment: Out On Friday has been unplaced in four of his last five starts, the exception a runner-up effort two starts back that stands out as the one bright spot; a 36-day absence since his latest run adds a further question over readiness.

runners_data.name: Blackjack Hills
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with two wins at 8-10f on Standard and Heavy, but a poor recent run at 10f on Good (seventh) and zero wins on this type of surface in the current dataset; a genuine hold-up type placed in the midfield on the map, his chance is tempered by both the going concern and the fade flag.
runners_data.comment: Blackjack Hills strung together back-to-back wins in his recent form, sandwiched by two earlier unplaced efforts and a below-par seventh last time out; the winning form is there in patches, but he rates the most modest of these nine on our figures.

races.paceDynamic: En Or is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival to push him through the early stages, he should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m2f trip. The field does contain more prominent-running types than the pace map can accommodate — Faro Island and Blackjack Hills are natural pace/prominent horses who are unlikely to secure those positions in this configuration, meaning En Or leads largely on his own terms. Daler, Unterberg, and Neo Smart will fill the prominent berths directly behind, but none has the profile to pressure En Or aggressively, keeping the tempo honest rather than fierce. A steady-to-moderate gallop run by a single uncontested leader over this distance on Good turf strongly favours hold-up horses who can produce a sustained finishing effort — Marmeladova's consistent good-ground form and Sinbad My Dad's stamina profile both fit that bill, provided they can find daylight off a contained pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: En Or Controls, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If En Or bowls along uncontested and sets a steady-moderate gallop that sets up a real finish in the straight.
scenarios.body: En Or dictates throughout without pressure and the race is run at a tempo that plays into the hands of hold-up horses with genuine finishing kicks over this distance. Marmeladova, with eight runs on Good ground and a solid recent placed record at 1m2f, is ideally positioned to pounce, while Sinbad My Dad's stamina could also come into play.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely slow and the prominent horses coast into a winning position without being overhauled.
scenarios.body: En Or and Daler settle close to the pace and never face a sustained challenge from behind, with the hold-up horses failing to close the gap from the rear in the straight. Daler, back up in distance after a winning effort at 9f on soft ground, could find this combination of trip and steady pace very much in his favour, while Unterberg's recent stamina form at 1m2f is also relevant.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Late Charge
scenarios.trigger: If En Or goes too quick early or the pace is uneven, causing prominent horses to tire and leaving the race wide open in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A collapse in the front-running effort creates a vacuum that genuine hold-up horses can exploit if they have covered the ground economically, though Out On Friday's noted tendency to fade makes him an unreliable beneficiary. Marmeladova again emerges as the most likely winner of this shape given her strong Good-ground record and the consistent placed efforts she has accumulated in recent months.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, No Clear Shape
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves unpredictable due to jostling among the prominent types and the race devolves into a messy, tactical affair.
scenarios.body: Multiple horses attempt to find a prominent position early, disrupting the expected settled rhythm and producing a race where class and adaptability matter most. Colin Keane's experience on Daler could prove decisive in a scrappy contest, and Marmeladova's tactical versatility under W J Lee may also help her navigate the trouble.

watchPoints.text: Marmeladova is the horse to watch in the straight — if En Or's uncontested lead produces the expected steady gallop, W J Lee will be angling her out for a run from the two-furlong pole and her Good-ground closing record makes her the most dangerous finisher.

En Or's 43-day absence and step back in trip from 14-16f to 1m2f is worth monitoring at the start — if he jumps sluggishly or surrenders the lead early, the entire pace dynamic collapses and the race becomes far less predictable.

Faro Island is a natural prominent runner forced into a midfield position by the race shape — watch whether Dylan Browne McMonagle attempts to push forward from the outset; if he does, it will increase pressure on En Or and meaningfully change the pace scenario.

Daler's viability in Scenario A depends entirely on whether he has the stamina to see out 1m2f on Good ground — his wins have come at 9-10f and if the pace is steady his prominent position could leave him vulnerable to closers in the final furlong.

Out On Friday's fade flag and double-figure finishes on Good ground at this trip suggest he is a horse to oppose rather than follow — if he appears to be travelling well at the two-furlong marker, treat it with caution given the pattern in his form.

races.name: BOYLE Sports Home Of The Early Payout Handicap

runners_data.name: Ob La Di
runners_data.note: Smart hold-up performer for JP Murtagh's yard with Ben Coen aboard; good ground clearly suits (two recent efforts on good), but the drop back from further trips and a pattern of finishing mid-pack (five-figure finishes) means she needs things to go perfectly late.|
runners_data.comment: Ob La Di is rated top of six on our figures at 84 with a useful speed figure of 83 to match, and already has the trip covered, even though her recent form (5th, 8th, 4th, two blanks) has been modest. Still without a win in that time, but on the figures alone she rates the one to catch.

runners_data.name: Cala Bonita
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner in the field and likely to bowl along in front unchallenged; won twice over 10f on standard going and recent form shows a bounce-back fourth, though racing from a prominent style when tagged STYLE_FIT means she could be flattered by the lack of pressure rather than winning on merit.|
runners_data.comment: Cala Bonita won successive starts four and five back and is rated third of six on our figures at 73, quick to back up just 5 days after her latest outing. A below-par eighth last time is the query, but the pair of wins in her locker make her the chief threat to the selection.

runners_data.name: Killyclogher Rose
runners_data.note: Won over 11f on good ground last time out — the best recent form in the race — and naturally prominent so she should slot in just behind the leader without a fight for position; the 22-day freshener looks fine and the trip is a slight step up, which her pedigree should handle.|
runners_data.comment: Killyclogher Rose won last time out and is rated fourth of six on our figures at 72, with the trip already proven. A modest speed figure of 62 is the concern, but the form is heading in the right direction on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Derry Lad
runners_data.note: Veteran of eight who carries a consistent finishing fade, flagged as a horse that doesn't see it out under pressure; hold-up style and a string of single-figure but beaten efforts suggest he needs something to go wrong ahead of him, and the headgear (tp) hasn't sparked a revival.|
runners_data.comment: Derry Lad is rated markedly higher on our figures (75) than his official mark of 67, despite a modest sequence of two fifths and two ninths in his last five starts. Still without a win in that time, but the gap between the two suggests more in the tank than the bare form shows.

runners_data.name: Tatum
runners_data.note: Strong recent form includes two wins and two places over 12-13f on good, making him the most talented horse here on a form reading; Dylan Browne McMonagle is an inspired booking, but as a true prominent type pushed into a midfield map position by a crowded pace profile, his chance is partly dependent on how much space opens up early.|
runners_data.comment: Tatum won two of her last five starts, including three starts back, and is rated fifth of six on our figures at 72. A moderate fifth last time and a 36-day absence are the concerns, but the pair of wins in that sequence show she retains real ability at this level.

runners_data.name: Cooley's Mist
runners_data.note: Trainer H Rogers in decent recent form (1 from 5 over 14 days) and Chris Hayes takes the ride; a natural front-runner who has been redistributed to midfield because the prominent berths are full, meaning he is likely to race out of his comfort zone — his STYLE_FIT discount is meaningful and his form figures in this company are moderate.|
runners_data.comment: Cooley's Mist is rated bottom of six on our figures at 71 and winless in his last five starts, though a pair of thirds in his last two starts shows he can find the frame. A useful speed figure of 82 hints at unexploited potential, but the formline itself offers little encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Cala Bonita is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press her, should control pace from the outset over this 1m5f trip at Leopardstown, creating a measured, sustainable gallop that suits those tracking close. Killyclogher Rose will look to sit prominently just behind, while the hold-up pair of Ob La Di and Derry Lad will need that gallop to sharpen late. The field holds more prominent-minded types than the map can accommodate — Tatum and Cooley's Mist are natural front-rank horses but, with Cala Bonita and Killyclogher Rose already filling those slots, both are likely to find themselves racing a position or two deeper than they would prefer. With one unchallenged pace-setter and a controlled tempo expected, this race shape strongly favours horses positioned prominently just off the leader — able to respond when the race ignites in the final two furlongs — rather than hold-up horses relying on a searching gallop that simply may not materialise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cala Bonita Controls, Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Cala Bonita sets a moderate unchallenged pace and the race is decided by those tracking closest into the straight.
scenarios.body: Cala Bonita dictates on her own terms and kicks turning for home, but the horses ranged immediately behind — particularly Killyclogher Rose — are ideally placed to pounce as the leader ties up; at 1m5f the trip tests Cala Bonita's stamina and those with a prominent stalking position reap the reward.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Finish Strong
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is deceptively honest and the closing stages open up for those coming from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Ob La Di, suited to good ground and operating over a staying trip, gets a clear run through and makes up ground late; Ben Coen's enterprise in the saddle could unlock a position earlier than the horse's natural style suggests, giving the hold-up brigade a genuine shot.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Cala Bonita Front-Runs And Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is truly pedestrian and Cala Bonita's lead becomes insurmountable before rivals can organise a challenge.
scenarios.body: Racing fresh off just a five-day turnaround and on going that suits, Cala Bonita is never headed and the chasing pack simply runs out of track; this scenario relies on the pace being too slow for any finisher to reel her in.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Pair Force Their Way Through
scenarios.trigger: If Tatum or Cooley's Mist manage to secure a forward position despite being mapped back and turn it into a race-winning advantage.
scenarios.body: Dylan Browne McMonagle's positive riding could push Tatum into a better spot than the map allows, leveraging his course-and-distance winning form over 13f on good ground; however, with both horses tagged out of their natural role, this remains the least likely scenario and their STYLE_FIT discount dampens expectation.

watchPoints.text: Killyclogher Rose's positioning is crucial — watch whether WJ Lee sends her forward quickly to lock onto Cala Bonita's heels, because if she does she is racing in the perfect slot for this shape.

Tatum's early move: if Dylan Browne McMonagle pushes forward aggressively from the gate to reclaim his natural prominent position ahead of Cooley's Mist, the pace dynamic could tighten and alter the tempo calculation entirely.
Cala Bonita ran just five days ago — monitor market moves for any sign of freshness concern; a tired front-runner setting a slow pace could paradoxically make it easier for hold-up types to close.

Derry Lad's fade flag is worth tracking at the 2f pole — if he is travelling well at that point it may signal the pace was slower than expected, but past patterns suggest he will be stopping when others are going.

Ob La Di's sim-going record is only 1W1P from 10 runs on comparable ground, meaning good ground alone does not guarantee her best — watch whether Ben Coen opts for a more forward position to compensate for the expected lack of pace.
